memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ...Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan... These are the sons of Shem by their clans and languages, in their territories and nations. - Gen 10:28-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The list continues with more names - Obal, Abimael, Jobab, and others - most of whom we know nothing about beyond their mention here. They lived, they had families, they were part of nations and territories, and then their stories faded from human memory. Yet here they are, preserved forever in the Word of God. Names the world has entirely forgotten are remembered by God.

This is quietly moving. Countless people have lived and died whose names no history book records, whose faces no one remembers, whose stories are utterly lost to us. But not to God. He knows every one. These forgotten names in an ancient genealogy remind us that no life is truly forgotten by the God who made it.

Perhaps you sometimes feel that your life is small and unremembered - that you work and love and serve in obscurity, unnoticed by the world. Take heart from these names. The God who recorded Obal and Jobab knows you too. Your life, however hidden, is fully known and remembered by Him.

And there is a greater book than any genealogy. For all who trust in Christ, their names are written in "the Lamb's book of life" (Rev 21:27) - never to be forgotten, never to be erased, remembered by God for all eternity. The world may forget you, but God never will. Live today not for the fleeting memory of people, but for the eternal remembrance of God, who knows your name and holds it dear.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you ever feel your life is unnoticed or unremembered?
- How does it comfort you that God remembers every life, including yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that no life is forgotten by You, however hidden or small. Thank You that in Christ my name is written in Your book of life forever. Help me live for Your remembrance, not the world's.
